card.name: The word both after a comma
card.fires_on: The word "both" (sometimes "many" or "a") placed after a comma or dash, right where a pair or two groups are about to be named. Found in general essay-style prose.

modes.label: Both after a comma
modes.description: "both" follows a comma or dash and introduces two paired items or groups.
modes.example: and with their rapid expansion under successive Israeli governments,<< both>> of the left and the right, are

modes.label: Many or a as a determiner
modes.description: "many" or "a" appears as a determiner before a noun or relative clause.
modes.example: that<< many>> Britons still felt in the eighteenth

card.writes: It slightly promotes the word "appropriate" and similar words, but the effect is weak and unclear.
card.plain: It fires on the word "both" when it opens a pairing after a comma, as in "both of the left and the right".
